steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: So you mean to say that Hoederer has failed?

steps.name: Sarkaz Warrior
steps.text: Yes, General. I saw it with my own eyes. He was gravely wounded in the battle just now.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: And he was in contact with another Sarkaz woman, aside from his longtime mercenary acquaintance?

steps.name: Sarkaz Warrior
steps.text: Right. But she's... highly skilled at concealment, and moves too quickly.

steps.name: Sarkaz Warrior
steps.text: I was anxious about getting too close. Couldn't shake the feeling she'd notice me with one wrong step.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Wise choice. You wouldn't have made it back alive otherwise.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: That said, I'm surprised the Confessarius let Babel's assassin go free. Was that an oversight, or their intent?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: ...No matter.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Tell me about Hoederer. Where is he?

steps.name: Sarkaz Warrior
steps.text: He's still marshaling the remaining mercenaries, and about to resume pursuing the escaped convicts.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Have him return. Those convicts will not stay free forever.

steps.name: Sarkaz Warrior
steps.text: General?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: As you said, his wounds are no laughing matter.

steps.name: Sarkaz Warrior
steps.text: Forgive me, but why do you still trust Hoederer so much?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: I've had you with him this whole time.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Correct me if I'm wrong, but you've never once reported any misdeeds from him.

steps.name: Sarkaz Warrior
steps.text: But he used to work for Babel!

steps.name: Sarkaz Warrior
steps.text: It was the mercenaries under his watch that screwed up, and it was his old friend that incited them! Don't you think it's too risky to keep him in such a key position, General?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: You've seen for yourself today. How does one Victorian regard another?

steps.name: Sarkaz Warrior
steps.text: Urgh...

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: And how much more difficult do you think it is for one Sarkaz to trust another?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: We've had everything stolen from us, been forced to grow accustomed to fighting each other for the right to survive.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: And now, we've obtained a new opportunity.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: You tell me, do you want to go back to monitoring a possible Sarkaz spy, or will you accompany me in eliminating the remaining Victorian threats?

steps.name: Sarkaz Warrior
steps.text: General, we choose to go with you.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: *pant*... *pant*... Did we shake them?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We can't let our guards down yet, Mr. Feist.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: I know... *huff*... I know.

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: ...Captain.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: What is it?

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: Your face is splattered in blood.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Blood?! Hey, Bill... Bill?

steps.name: Bill
steps.text: Nrgh...

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: ...Oh, it's just my own blood. No need to panic, then.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Come on, Bill, you could breathe a little louder! I don't want to have spent all this effort porting a dead man back.

steps.name: Bill
steps.text: Then think about... swinging your spanner gentler.

steps.name: Bill
steps.text: You're always... hitting me... in the head...

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: I hear you. You're the boss today.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Hold on a little longer... we'll be right back home soon. Right? I'm not going blind, am I?

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: Eugh, this blood from my forehead's getting in my eyes a little... Rockrock, eyes out. How much left to our target rendezvous?

steps.name: Rockrock
steps.text: A little over 300 meters and we're there.

steps.name: Feist
steps.text: It's Team 6 on guard here, right? I could really use a hand from them. Bill, old bud, you're getting harder to carry by the second.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: ...How long have we gone without a signal from the surface team?

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Didn't the Doctor say they'd only contact us after they reach that last RDV?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: No, I mean the Self-Salvation Corps, at the one before that.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: We had an agreement that they'd keep us up to date with the surface situation every half hour.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Shit, I wasn't tracking the time! How long's it been?

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: ...We need to go up and see.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: No!

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: If the Sarkaz have already discovered our last rendezvous, then the Doctor's squad is in danger. You're clearly worried sick about Morgan and Dagda too.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: A... And you too!

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Worst comes to worst, Vina, I go peek, and you stay here. Suppose somehow something's happened, you scarper further in...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Indra, I can't always keep cowering behind you all. First our mentor, then you and the Glasgow Gang, now the Doctor—

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: —I've cowered for far too long, and I know it. Dagda wasn't talking nonsense. If you're always tucked away in the shadows, you gradually lose the courage to directly face the sun.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: She's trying to nark you! You know what she's dying for? You, taking her to storm the Palace, and finding that what's-his-gent to do him in!

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: And you're itching to go back to the Glasgow Gang. Don't you understand her point of view?

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: I... Like hell I don't, but that's the bloody thing. I understand, and that's why...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: You're scared she'll end up killing herself, the way she rushes it.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: You can bloody imagine, can't you? She's got a death wish in my eyes, the way she acts!

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: ...You need to trust her.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: She'll be willing to live for our sake... and the sake of so many, even if it comes with enormous pain.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: She's an outstanding knight, and a warrior of Victoria. She has everything in common with the countless others who struggle to live, and fight on for Victoria.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: And I... I have to fight with them. Not because I'm in some special position, but because we're all 'native' to this land.

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Vina...

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Think of that commander, Lady Clovisia. Would she abandon her soldiers, run off just to keep herself safe?

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: I'm not familiar with her... but I don't imagine she would. Those soldiers really trust in her.

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Then in your eyes, how much do I pale in comparison?

steps.name: Indra
steps.text: Like bloody hell you pale at all!

steps.name: Siege
steps.text: Then follow me. Together, we'll make sure that our comrades-in-arms have a safe trip home.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: We finally get to leave this stinking place soon.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Are you alright, 'Spy'?

steps.name: Taran Secret Agent
steps.text: ...Whoof... *huff*... I'm fine, Mandragora.

steps.name: Taran Secret Agent
steps.text: The last few times I've heard the word 'spy' it's been from a Sarkaz thinking up some fresh new punishment. I almost forgot it was my codename.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Then pick a more tasteful one next time, if you have the chance. 'The Elocutionist' and all that lot had good ones, and they kicked the bucket without leaving so much as a smear.

steps.name: Taran Secret Agent
steps.text: Haha...

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Save your strength for now. The Leader still needs the Sarkaz intel you found.

steps.name: Taran Secret Agent
steps.text: You mean... The Shard...

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: No, don't say it.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Not like I don't want to hear, but... we need the Leader's approval. Our soldiers are all clean sorts. Don't go giving them too big a burden to carry.

steps.name: Taran Secret Agent
steps.text: I understand... Mandragora... you've always been such a good girl.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Don't sweet-talk me like 'The Bandit' did. Sick of it. They're all gone and now I'm stuck here alone in this shithole having to worry about the Leader.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: At least you got back quick. While you were gone, that Harmonie bastard was glued to the Leader's side day and night, and I was terrified that... that...

steps.name: Taran Secret Agent
steps.text: Terrified... that what?

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: That the Leader would get too close to those noble sorts, and that someday, she'd have no more use for us.

steps.name: Taran Secret Agent
steps.text: The Leader, eh... *sigh*...

steps.name: Dublinn Soldier
steps.text: Ma'am, I've ascertained the others' positions. They're still in the same place, watching the door for the Sarkaz. Are we linking up with them right now?

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Mm. Get the paramedics going. 'The Spy' needs immediate treatment.

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Right, one more thing. Find a Messenger and notify Count Mourning outside the city immediately. We have to ensure 'The Spy' meets the Leader as soon as possible.

steps.name: Taran Secret Agent
steps.text: Count Mourning? You... involved him for the Leader?

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: Tch. Times like these, we have no choice but to hope the nobles do something to help. Funny kind of joke, isn't it?

steps.name: Taran Secret Agent
steps.text: *cough* *cough*... You... You've grown well...

steps.name: Mandragora
steps.text: That's not like you, 'Spy'. You're speaking too much rubbish. Save the rest for when you're not ragged enough to drop dead at a stiff breeze.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: ...Hold it.

steps.name: Robben
steps.text: What is it, Horn? We have a visual on the exit already.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Mind the perimeter.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Three o'clock!

steps.name: Robben
steps.text: Horn, it's Sarkaz!

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Robben, are you still fine for ammo?

steps.name: Robben
steps.text: Ha... haha... sorry, Horn. Truth is, I've been hiding an explosive shell on me.

steps.name: Robben
steps.text: All this time, I've had it in my head that if I fall into the enemy's hands at some point again... I'll be taking this shell with me to my last stand.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: ...Shame, we improvised that shell ourselves.

steps.name: Robben
steps.text: How's that got anything to do with—

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: And I'm very sorry, but I'm not inclined to give you that opportunity.

steps.name: Robben
steps.text: Eh? My shell—

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Looks like the power of a homemade one falls a bit short after all.

steps.name: Robben
steps.text: But... but he's unscathed, how?

steps.name: Robben
steps.text: That Sarkaz...

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: That Sarkaz is their beloved General.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: We finally meet. An improvised shell is hardly a suitable greeting though.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: I know you've met your share of Victorian soldiers, Sarkaz. After all, a great deal of them died by your hands. I imagine their spirits are practically lining up to crowd your dreams.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: No need to be so self-effacing, White Wolf of Victoria.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Even to the Sarkaz, you qualify as a heroic warrior.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: As I recall, the captain who rendered Kazdel a sea of flames once more, two hundred years ago, was your ancestor.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Are you some monster who's lived for centuries too?

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: I had no chance to witness that war.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: But listen to the way you talk about it. It's no different from your kin who feed on others' lives to prolong their own.

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: 'Those stained in Sarkaz blood must pay that blood back, thousands of times over.'

steps.name: Manfred
steps.text: Where do you think we came from, Victorian? Just who runs in fear at the restless souls circling Londinium's skies day and night, murmuring their blood feuds?

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Did you know? I became a professional soldier precisely because I was fed up with justifying this war we're in.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: Come, Sarkaz.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: The words of the deceased lingering about my ears are more than you'll ever hear.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: And I promised them... I promised them this.

steps.name: Horn
steps.text: I will not fall until I see my people out of this place alive.
